statement: You have an n × n chessboard and n queens. A queen attacks every square in its row, its column and both of its diagonals.
Place all n queens so that no two of them attack each other. Two placements are different if some square holds a queen in one and not in the other.
Given n, return the number of different placements.

examples.explanation: On a 4 × 4 board the only non-attacking placements put the queens in columns 2, 4, 1, 3 of rows 1 to 4, or the mirror image 3, 1, 4, 2.
A 5 × 5 board has 10 non-attacking placements; the backtracking search abandons a row as soon as every column in it is attacked.
